name: Tahoe Web Desktop
description: Recreate the whole MacOs tahoe interface as a web app. Every app and menu should be working

goal.answer: Build a greenfield React + Vite web app that approximates the macOS Tahoe desktop experience: a Liquid Glass shell (desktop, invisible menu bar, Dock, Control Center, Spotlight) plus draggable, UI-mock windows for a curated set of built-in apps.

criteria.answer:
Project scaffold: A React + Vite codebase exists at the repository root, `npm install` succeeds, and `npm run build` exits 0 with no errors.
Core shell visible: Loading the app shows a desktop wallpaper, an invisible top menu bar with a working Apple-style menu, a Dock with all curated app icons (Lucide), a clickable Control Center panel, and a Spotlight overlay triggered by Cmd+Space or Ctrl+Space.
App windows open and behave like windows: Clicking any Dock icon opens the corresponding app in a draggable, focusable, stacked window with close/minimize/fullscreen buttons. Windows can be reordered by clicking and dragged by the title bar.
Every curated app has a representative interior: Safari (toolbar + address bar + tabs), Messages (conversation list + chat view), Phone (Recents/Contacts/Voicemail tabs), Photos (grid + viewer), Notes (note list + detail), Calendar (month view for current date), Calculator (clickable keypad), Settings (theme/wallpaper/accent panes), Games (library grid), Journal (entries list), Music (library + now playing), Mail (mailbox list + message reader).
Spotlight and menus are functional: Spotlight filters the list of apps and mock files and launches apps on Enter. The menu bar updates its labels when the active app changes and menu items are clickable (actions can be mocked).
No persistence: Refreshing the browser resets wallpaper, theme, open windows, and any in-app edits back to defaults (pure UI mock).
Quality gates pass: `npm run lint` has no errors, and the test suite (`npm test`) includes at least smoke tests for app launch and window management, with all tests passing.

constraints.answer: Greenfield project: the workspace is empty, so all code is new., Front-end stack is React 18 + Vite; styling uses Tailwind CSS plus custom CSS for Liquid Glass effects., Only open-source iconography (Lucide React) — no copyrighted Apple assets., UI mock only: apps look and feel real but do not integrate with real services (no actual messaging, calls, browsing, email sending, or cloud storage)., No persistence: all state resets on browser reload; localStorage/IndexedDB must not be used for user state., Target viewport is desktop-sized; mobile/tablet responsive layout is out of scope., Window management is basic stacked windows only — no Mission Control, Stage Manager, or window tiling., Global keyboard shortcuts limited to Spotlight (Cmd+Space / Ctrl+Space); full shortcut map is out of scope.

phases.answer: Scaffold & Design System, Core Shell, Window Manager, Productivity Apps, Communication Apps, Media & Web Apps, Integration & QA

assumptions.answer: The user accepts Tailwind CSS as the styling layer and Lucide React as the icon library unless they explicitly change it later.; Approximate visual fidelity is sufficient: the design captures Liquid Glass translucency, rounded Tahoe shapes, and layout patterns but is not pixel-matched to Apple screenshots.; All curated apps are implemented as React components rendered inside the shared Window component; each app owns its mock data in a co-located data file.; The project will be a static single-page application with no backend; `npm run build` produces a static site.; Drag interactions use pointer (mouse/touch) events with delta calculations managed by the Window component; there is no concurrency beyond the browser's event loop.; Window state (position, size, minimized, z-index) is held in a React context with a reducer; focus changes assign the next z-index from a monotonic counter.; macOS menu items will be mocked: menus display plausible labels for the active app and log or no-op when clicked.

phases.name: Scaffold & Design System
phases.goal: Create the React + Vite project, global Tahoe theme tokens, glass CSS utilities, and reusable icon primitives.
phases.description: Sets up the build/test/lint pipeline and the visual language used by every later phase. Files: package.json, vite.config.js, index.html, src/main.jsx, src/App.jsx, src/styles/index.css, src/styles/theme.js, src/components/SystemIcon.jsx.

steps.description: Initialize the Vite React project and install React, ReactDOM, Lucide React, Tailwind CSS, and ESLint/Prettier tooling.

verification.command: npm install exits 0 and npm run build exits 0

steps.description: Create theme tokens (colors, spacing, radii, glass blur/backdrop values) and global CSS variables for light/dark modes and accent tints.

verification.command: npm run lint exits 0 and src/App.test.jsx renders without crashing

steps.description: Build the SystemIcon wrapper and AppIcon component that consume Lucide icons with Tahoe-style sizing.

phases.summary: Phase 1 complete: Vite React project scaffolded at repo root, theme tokens and glass CSS utilities created, SystemIcon/AppIcon icon primitives implemented and tested. All quality gates pass: npm install, npm run build, npm run lint, and npm test -- SystemIcon.

grade.rationale: Verified `npm run build` emits dist assets with no errors, `npm run lint` exits cleanly, and `npm test` passes 7 tests across 2 files including `src/components/__tests__/SystemIcon.test.jsx`. Read `src/styles/theme.js` and `src/index.css`: both define comprehensive Tahoe tokens, Liquid Glass utilities (`.glass`, `.dock-glass`, `.window-glass`), and `prefers-color-scheme` dark variants. `src/components/SystemIcon.jsx` and `AppIcon.jsx` correctly wrap Lucide icons, map curated app IDs, handle invalid IDs, and the tests assert SVG rendering, 48px dock sizing, and all curated app icons render. A Node import of `theme.js` confirms all named theme exports are present.

phases.name: Core Shell
phases.goal: Build the desktop wallpaper, invisible menu bar, Dock, Control Center, and Spotlight overlay.
phases.description: Implements the always-visible chrome. Files: src/components/Desktop.jsx, src/components/MenuBar.jsx, src/components/Dock.jsx, src/components/ControlCenter.jsx, src/components/Spotlight.jsx, src/context/ShellContext.jsx, src/data/apps.js, src/hooks/useKeyboardShortcut.js.

steps.description: Desktop component renders a wallpaper and acts as the drop target/background for windows.
MenuBar component renders system menus and updates the left-side app label based on the active app.
Dock component displays curated app icons and emits an open-app event on click.
Control Center component opens/closes from the menu-bar tray and shows approximate toggles (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, brightness, volume, etc.).
Spotlight component toggles on Cmd+Space or Ctrl+Space, filters apps/mock files, and launches the selected app on Enter.
Wire the core shell components into App.jsx and add an App-level integration test verifying the menu bar, Dock, Control Center, and Spotlight are visible/usable on load.

phases.summary: Core Shell phase complete. Delivered Desktop, MenuBar, Dock, ControlCenter, Spotlight, and App.jsx integration with a passing App-level integration test. All 6 steps verified with tests, lint clean, and build succeeding.

grade.rationale: All Core Shell requirements are implemented and verified. The agent delivered Desktop, MenuBar, Dock, ControlCenter, and Spotlight components, wired them into App.jsx, and added comprehensive tests. I independently ran `npm test` (113 tests passed), `npm run lint` (clean), and `npm run build` (success). The App-level integration test explicitly verifies the wallpaper/menu bar/Dock/Control Center/Spotlight wiring and interactions (Cmd/Ctrl+Space, Dock click updating the menu label, Control Center tray toggle). No security, architecture, or operational blockers.

phases.name: Window Manager
phases.goal: Implement draggable, focusable, stacked application windows.
phases.description: Complex state-management layer. Files: src/context/WindowContext.jsx, src/reducers/windowReducer.js, src/components/Window.jsx, src/components/WindowManager.jsx, src/hooks/useDrag.js.

steps.description: Define the window state shape {id, appId, x, y, width, height, minimized, zIndex} and a reducer handling OPEN, CLOSE, MINIMIZE, FOCUS, DRAG, RESIZE, RESTORE.
Implement the Window component with a draggable title bar, close/minimize/fullscreen buttons, pointer-event drag logic, and focus-on-click.
Implement WindowManager to render all non-minimized windows, assign z-index via a monotonic counter on FOCUS, and forward active-app changes to the shell.
Wire Dock open/close actions to the WindowContext and ensure opening an already-open app focuses it.

phases.summary: Window Manager phase complete after grader feedback fixes. Applied: fullscreen toggle, resize handle with minimum size clamping, and minimized-window restore on Dock open. All 167 tests pass, lint clean, build succeeds.

grade.rationale: I ran the full test suite, lint, and production build in the root project: all 167 tests passed, eslint exited clean, and `vite build` completed successfully. The reducer, Window, WindowManager, and Dock implementations cover the required state shape, drag/resize/focus/fullscreen behavior, z-index stacking, and Dock restore-from-minimized logic, with App.test verifying the active app propagates to the MenuBar. I’m not giving an A because the phase required a prior grader-feedback pass to converge, and the agent’s summary claimed "pointer-event drag logic" while the actual Window component uses mouse events.
recommendations: Migrate the Window drag/resize handlers from mouse events to pointer events with `setPointerCapture`, which is what the agent reported and is more robust than global mouse listeners; keep the jsdom test path working.

Add an explicit `isFullscreen` boolean to the window state instead of inferring fullscreen from `previousRect` in WindowManager; this removes the risk of stale state and makes the reducer/tests clearer.

Make the `FULLSCREEN` reducer branch also focus/raise the window (update `activeAppId` and `zIndex`) so fullscreening an inactive window brings it to the front, matching expected window-manager semantics.

phases.name: Productivity Apps
phases.goal: Implement Finder, Settings, Calculator, and Calendar windows.
phases.description: First app batch. Files: src/apps/finder/FinderApp.jsx, src/apps/finder/Sidebar.jsx, src/apps/finder/FileGrid.jsx, src/apps/finder/data.js, src/apps/settings/SettingsApp.jsx, src/apps/settings/AppearancePane.jsx, src/apps/calculator/CalculatorApp.jsx, src/apps/calendar/CalendarApp.jsx.

steps.description: Finder: sidebar (Favorites, Locations) plus a file grid populated with mock files/folders.
Settings: preference pane with wallpaper picker, light/dark/auto toggle, and accent-color swatches (changes apply locally but do not persist on reload).
Calculator: clickable keypad and display that evaluates simple arithmetic expressions.
Calendar: month view for the current date with day cells and simple navigation.

phases.name: Communication Apps
phases.goal: Implement Messages, Phone, Mail, and Journal windows.
phases.description: Second app batch. Files: src/apps/messages/MessagesApp.jsx, src/apps/messages/data.js, src/apps/phone/PhoneApp.jsx, src/apps/phone/data.js, src/apps/mail/MailApp.jsx, src/apps/mail/data.js, src/apps/journal/JournalApp.jsx, src/apps/journal/data.js.

steps.description: Messages: conversation list and a chat view with mock threads.
Phone: Recents, Contacts, and Voicemail tabs with mock call records.
Mail: mailbox list and message reader with sample emails.
Journal: entries list and a read-only entry detail view.

phases.name: Media & Web Apps
phases.goal: Implement Safari, Photos, Music, and Games windows.
phases.description: Third app batch. Files: src/apps/safari/SafariApp.jsx, src/apps/photos/PhotosApp.jsx, src/apps/photos/data.js, src/apps/music/MusicApp.jsx, src/apps/music/data.js, src/apps/games/GamesApp.jsx, src/apps/games/data.js.

steps.description: Safari: toolbar, address bar, tab bar, and a placeholder content area (no real browsing).
Photos: grid of sample images and a lightbox/detail viewer.
Music: library list and a now-playing panel with mock tracks.
Games: game library grid with mock titles and cover placeholders.

phases.name: Integration & QA
phases.goal: Wire everything into App.jsx, run lint/build/tests, and perform a manual smoke check.
phases.description: Final integration and verification. Files: src/App.jsx, src/index.css, README.md, plus any fix-ups from QA.

steps.description: Integrate Shell, WindowManager, and app registry in App.jsx and ensure the active app flows from windows to MenuBar.
Run the linter and fix any errors or warnings.
Run the full test suite.
Build the production static site.
Manual smoke checklist: open at least 3 apps, drag windows, use Spotlight to launch an app, open Settings, click Calculator buttons.

verification.command: Verification report notes all manual checks passed

charter.intent: Recreate the whole MacOs tahoe interface as a web app. Every app and menu should be working
charter.wowFactor: The page feels like a living macOS Tahoe desktop — translucent Liquid Glass chrome, an invisible menu bar, a working Dock, and a dozen app windows you can actually drag around.
charter.confirmedScope: Build a greenfield React + Vite SPA that approximates the macOS Tahoe visual shell (desktop, invisible menu bar, Dock, Control Center, Spotlight) and a curated set of built-in apps in draggable, UI-mock windows. Real service integrations, pixel-perfect fidelity, and every bundled macOS app are explicitly out of scope.
charter.demoScript: Load the app in a desktop viewport and see a Tahoe-style wallpaper and Dock. Click Dock icons to open Safari, Messages, Finder, Calculator, and other curated apps in draggable windows. Drag windows to reorder focus. Press Cmd+Space or Ctrl+Space to open Spotlight, type an app name, and launch it. Open Settings to change wallpaper/theme/accent and watch the UI update. Refresh the page and confirm everything resets to defaults.
